## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The header check is correct, and `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers it. The only correction found is optional: `test_rejects_legacy_header` should actually test a legacy header, because as written it cannot fail.

## Changes
`parse_report` now accepts only the exact header `REPORT v1`, where it previously accepted any line starting with `REPORT `. The pull request also adds two rejection tests.

## Suggestions
- tests/test_report.py:10 — tests — Make test_rejects_legacy_header use a v0 header — `rsplit("v1", 1)` replaces only the last `v1`, so the input becomes `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`. That input keeps the v1 header and has no `END` line. `parse_report` returns `None` at `app/report.py:3`, before the version check runs. The comment at line 9 says the test changes "the fixture's version to v0", but the header is unchanged. — This test would still pass if the version check were removed, so it gives a false signal about legacy-header coverage. — Fix: Use a complete fixture such as `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or delete this test because `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that case.
